instagram_caption:
Jaws is scary because its shark kept breaking. 🦈

In 1974, 27-year-old Steven Spielberg was shooting his first big studio film off Martha's Vineyard. The crew built three mechanical sharks, nicknamed Bruce after his lawyer. In salt water they rarely worked. A 55-day shoot ran to 159, and the budget more than doubled.

So he suggested the shark instead: yellow barrels, shots from under the water, and two low notes from John Williams (which he first thought were too simple). Jaws opened in June 1975 and became the first film to pass $100 million in America.

Spielberg has called the breakdowns 'just good fortune'. He has also said he had nightmares about the shoot for years, and that he still doesn't love swimming in the ocean.

The three sharks were dumped on a back lot and rotted away. A fourth, cast from the same mould, hung at Universal Studios, then sat in a junkyard for 25 years. Restored, it now hangs in the Academy Museum, where Spielberg thanked it for his career in 2025. That shark was never in the film.
